{{Short description|Mathematical notion}}
{{Wiktionary|anafunctor}}

In mathematics, an '''anafunctor'''{{refn|group=note|The etymology of anafunctor is an analogy of the biological terms [[anaphase]]/[[prophase]].{{R|Roberts2011}}}} is a notion introduced by {{harvtxt|Makkai|1996}} for ordinary categories that is a generalization of functors.{{R|Roberts2011}} In [[category theory]], some statements require the [[axiom of choice]], but the axiom of choice can sometimes be avoided when using an anafunctor.<ref name=Makkai1998>{{harv|Makkai|1998}}</ref> For example, the statement "every fully faithful and [[essentially surjective functor]] is an [[equivalence of categories]]" is equivalent to the axiom of choice, but we can usually follow the same statement without the axiom of choice by using  anafunctor instead of functor.{{R|Roberts2011}}<ref>{{harv|anafunctor in nlab|loc=§1. Idea}}</ref>

== Definition ==
=== Span formulation of anafunctors ===
[[File:Anafunctor (span).svg|thumb|Anafunctor (span)]]
Let {{mvar|X}} and {{mvar|A}} be [[Category (mathematics)|categories]]. An anafunctor {{mvar|F}} with domain ([[Morphism#Definition|source]]) {{mvar|X}} and [[codomain]] ([[Morphism#Definition|target]]) {{mvar|A}}, and between categories {{mvar|X}} and {{mvar|A}} is a category <math>|F|</math>, in a notation <math>F:X \xrightarrow{a} A</math>, is given by the following conditions:<ref name=Roberts2011>{{harv|Roberts|2011}}</ref><ref>{{harv|Makkai|1996|loc = §1.1. and 1.1*. Anafunctors }}</ref><ref>{{harv|Palmgren|2008|loc=§2. Anafunctors}}</ref><ref>{{harv|Schreiber|Waldorf|2007|loc=§7.4. Anafunctors}}</ref><ref>{{harv|anafunctor in nlab|loc=§2. Definitions}}</ref>

*<math>F_0</math> is surjective on [[Object of a category|object]]s.

*Let pair <math>F_0:|F| \rightarrow X</math> and <math>F_1:|F| \rightarrow A</math> be [[functor]]s, a [[Span (category theory)|span]] of ordinary functors (<math>X \leftarrow |F| \rightarrow A</math>), where <math>F_0</math> is [[Full and faithful functors|fully faithful]].

===Set-theoretic definition===
{{multiple image
 | direction = vertical
 | width = 180
 | image1 = Commutative diagram for morphism.svg
 | image2 = Commutative diagram for morphism 2.svg
 | footer = (5)
}}

An anafunctor <math>F: X \xrightarrow{a} A</math> following condition:{{R|Makkai1998}}<ref>{{harv|Makkai|1996|loc=§1.1. Anafunctor}}</ref><ref>{{harv|anafunctor in nlab|loc=§2. Anafunctors (Explicit set-theoretic definition)}}</ref>

#A set <math>|F|</math> of specifications of <math>F</math>, with maps <math>\sigma : |F| \to \mathrm{Ob} (X)</math> (source), <math>\tau : |F| \to \mathrm{Ob} (A)</math> (target). <math>|F|</math> is the set of specifications, <math>s \in |F|</math> specifies the value <math>\tau (s)</math> at the argument <math>\sigma (s)</math>. For <math>X \in \mathrm{Ob} (X)</math>, we write <math>|F| \; X</math> for the class <math>\{s \in |F| : \sigma (s) = X\}</math> and <math>F_{s} (X)</math> for <math>\tau (s)</math> the notation <math>F_{s} (X)</math> presumes that <math>s \in |F| \; X</math>.
#For each <math>X, \; Y \in \mathrm{Ob} (X)</math>, <math>x \in |F| \; X</math>, <math>y \in |F| \; Y</math> and <math>f : X \to Y</math> in the class of all arrows <math>\mathrm{Arr (X)}</math> an [[morphism|arrows]] <math>F_{x,y} (f) : F_{x} (X) \to F_{y} (Y)</math> in <math>A</math>.
#For every <math>X \in \mathrm{Ob} (X)</math>, such that <math>|F| \; X</math> is [[Inhabited set|inhabited]] (non-[[Empty set|empty]]).
#<math>F</math> hold [[Identity morphism|identity]]. For all <math>X \in \mathrm{Ob} (X)</math> and <math>x \in |F| \; X</math>, we have <math>F_{x,x} (\mathrm{id}_x) = \mathrm{id}_{F_{x}X}</math>
#<math>F</math> hold [[Morphism#Definition|composition]]. Whenever <math>X, Y, Z \in \mathrm{Ob} (X)</math>, <math>x \in |F|  \; X</math>, <math>y \in |F| \; Y</math>, <math>z \in |F| \; Z,</math> and <math>F_{x,z} (gf) = F_{y,z} (g) \circ F_{x,y} (f)
</math>.
